title: Consumer protection visibility, attention cost, remedy labels, and exit remain different endpoints
source_unit: Deliberately non-pooled CFPB complaint records, SHED household fraud reports, Pew platform/AI surveys, and FTC institutional inquiry

denominator.unit: 2025 published complaint records; annual denominators range from 444,837 in 2020 to 5,452,107 in 2025

observations.method: CFPB public complaint records aggregated by year with response, relief, and narrative fields; annual index composition and field definitions are retained as a measurement boundary.
observations.uncertainty: Complaint records are not consumer-harm rates, account denominators, verified remedy probabilities, or trust measures. Product mix, routing, publication, coding, and index changes may drive the shifts.
observations.subgroup: Published complaint records by calendar year; product and firm composition varies across years.
observations.counterinterpretation: More non-monetary response labels or fewer narratives can reflect administrative coding or routing rather than improved or worsened consumer welfare.

denominator.unit: published 2025 debt-collection records; other displayed product denominators include 84,348 checking/savings, 90,157 credit-card, 24,735 mortgage, 21,333 student-loan, and 20,823 vehicle-loan records

observations.method: Product-filtered CFPB complaint route extraction preserving explanation, relief, timeliness, narrative, and product-specific record denominators.
observations.uncertainty: The fields measure complaint processing and company-response labels, not account-level harm, remedy adequacy, repayment continuity, switching, or exit. Timeliness fields are not interchangeable across products.
observations.subgroup: Six financial-product complaint slices; each has a separate record universe and response mix.
observations.counterinterpretation: A high explanation share may be useful or inadequate; a low monetary-relief label may reflect issue type or coding rather than failed remedy.

observations.period: 2024; SHED household fraud, recovery, and time burden

denominator.unit: weighted adult population estimate; loss and recovery outcomes conditional on non-credit-card fraud

non_card_lost_money.unit: percent of adults experiencing non-credit-card fraud

some_not_recovered.unit: percent of adults experiencing non-credit-card fraud

ten_plus_hours.unit: percent of adults experiencing non-credit-card fraud

observations.method: Federal Reserve SHED 2024 weighted survey estimates preserving overlapping exposure categories and conditional loss/recovery/time universes.
observations.uncertainty: Self-reported most-recent-incident measures do not establish verified fraud, complete incidence, exact event recovery, firm liability, or causal trust/exit effects.
observations.subgroup: All adults and non-credit-card fraud reporters; categories and denominators are not interchangeable with CFPB complaints.
observations.counterinterpretation: Money may be recovered while attention, time, confidence, or institutional trust remain damaged; consumer-liability protections may reduce direct loss in some credit-card cases.

observations.period: 2025-2026; platform/AI use, privacy concern, civic exposure, and institutional inquiry

denominator.unit: US adult Pew survey respondents for February 2026 chatbot items; separate 2025 adult, teen, news, and FTC inquiry universes

ftc_companies_inquiry.unit: companies receiving FTC Section 6(b) information-gathering orders

observations.method: Non-pooled Pew adult/teen platform and AI surveys, Pew news-source and engagement typology, and FTC Section 6(b) AI-companion inquiry record.
observations.uncertainty: Use, concern, confidence, news exposure, civic typology, and an institutional inquiry have distinct samples and estimands. Practical usefulness can coexist with concern; inquiry is information gathering, not a finding or remedy.
observations.subgroup: US adults, teens, employed adults for selected work items, and seven companies under FTC inquiry; subgroup denominators differ.
observations.counterinterpretation: High use does not prove dependence or loss of control, and privacy concern does not identify a specific product loss, consumer exit, or political effect.

related_sources.claim: SHED household fraud loss, recovery, and time-cost source.
Pew AI use, privacy, and regulation-confidence source.

boundary: This is a non-pooled consumer visibility, attention, remedy, and exit architecture. It does not establish complaint incidence, verified remedy, consumer welfare, platform dependence, trust change, political action, or causal regulatory effect. A same-case or linked account panel from exposure through effort, decision, remedy, switching, trust, and exit remains open.
